A chain that shares the run and ends at the vertex, or whose two sides the batch leaves different, therefore clears the flag although the run it split survives whole: a STRETCH of C removed that ends at C's own point v on A's run, a REKEY of C whose cut is at v, and a RIDER B along A on one side ending at a crossing or T at v whose other chain is then removed. In each case the flag is cleared, and once C (K, or B) is gone v stays on A for ever and A is never restored (CONFIRMED on the design head e5029a5f: probes p1-forms.base.log F1 - F4, p4-pins.log Q1 - Q4 and Q6; the review's p6-writers.log 8 and 7 vertices against A alone's 6).

amendment.item: 1006 is rewritten and one item is added - numbered 1007 if the file's numbering is kept (1006 stays 'what is not settled'):
amendment.1007:
**1007.** **A run survives with a row in common** (the base section 2.2 rule 3, demotion (b) *flags*: "a pair of its incident edges of its lowest incident level that carried identical rows of that level before the batch still exists after it, at one level, with identical rows (a crossing has two such pairs, a T-junction one)" becomes:)

> a pair of its incident edges of its lowest incident level, on a run it split, is after the batch two edges of one level that carry a row of that level in common — the run's own row, whatever else rides along on either side, a row the batch wrote on both sides (a rekey) counting (a crossing has two such pairs, a T-junction one) — so a chain along the run that ends at the vertex, a stretch of it removed up to the vertex, a rekey cut there, or a rider beside it leaves the flag, and the run is restored once the rest goes
amendment.1006: In 1006's first sentence the clause 'a chain removed in TWO steps along a shared run — a stretch that ENDS at such a point, or a rekey cut there, clears the point's flag under rule 3 (b)'s whole-row-set comparison, so the point stays on the other chain once the rest is removed (Q181: a ruling on rule 3 (b) is owed; it predates this file);' is deleted (settled by 1007), and the kin stay: 'the reverse order (the chain first, another along it later), three coincident chains with the base removed first, a run whose two sides are of different levels before the batch (a coarse run's stretch removed up to the vertex, a finer chain along both sides), and a finer chain's crossing of a coarser one once the coarser is removed (the same canonical-form class, N-13)'.
amendment.997: In 997's last sentence 'The guard is stated for a chain inserted onto another chain's run and removed whole or by a stretch through the point.' becomes 'The guard is stated for a chain inserted onto another chain's run and removed whole, by a stretch through or ending at the point, or rekeyed with its cut there (rule 3 (b) keeps the flag while the other chain's row is on both sides, 1007).'
